description: Multi-hop question answering dataset for ZMWiki baseline vs experiment comparison. Built over a fictional company wiki (Acme Corp) with 9 interlinked pages. 50 questions (26 original cases mh01-mh30 plus 24 extension cases mh31-mh54); answers require combining information across 1-5 pages. Standard answers and keyword groups are used only by the evaluator, never passed to the system under test. Some cases annotate complete alternative evidence paths; evidence recall uses the best legal path. Extension cases add optional difficulty, reasoning_chain, relation_edges/attribute_lookups/reasoning_hops, answer_bindings/binding_entities, relation_chain, ratio_checks, comparison_checks, fabrication_patterns, fabrication_patterns_positive, manual_review, and distractor evidence annotations; the loader and evaluator ignore unknown fields, so the schema remains backward compatible.
link_construction: WikiPage links_to/links_from are manually verified from source document content, NOT produced by WikiCompiler. WikiCompiler currently leaves links_to empty; this dataset uses hand-built linked pages to evaluate follow_links capability. This is explicitly recorded as a capability gap of the current compiler.

_field_definitions.hops: Number of required evidence pages (len(required_page_ids)); NOT the number of graph relation edges.
_field_definitions.relation_edges: Number of entity-to-entity relation traversals such as reports_to, leads, manages, contributes_to, located_in, connected_to.
_field_definitions.attribute_lookups: Number of terminal scalar attribute lookups such as title, tenure, budget, deadline, team size, degree, tech stack, responsibilities.
_field_definitions.reasoning_hops: relation_edges + attribute_lookups; the evidence-binding step count recorded in reasoning_chain.
_field_definitions.answer_bindings: Entity-bound attribute checks; binding_entities bounds each subject's clause by other entity mentions.
_field_definitions.relation_chain: Ordered chain plus direct/indirect relation checks.
_field_definitions.ratio_checks: Bounded n:d ratio recognition; a bare numerator is accepted only when allow_bare is true.
_field_definitions.comparison_checks: Directed greater/less comparison: the greater marker must bind the left entity before the right, or the less marker must bind the right before the left.
_field_definitions.fabrication_patterns: Regex guards for unanswerable cases; heuristic, not a complete hallucination detector.
_field_definitions.fabrication_patterns_positive: Regex guards that skip matches surrounded by negation, so a refusal may mention a true related fact without being treated as fabrication.
_field_definitions.manual_review: True when the automatic score is heuristic and a human should audit the case.

question_type_taxonomy.three_plus_hop_chain: Requires at least three consecutive knowledge relations across three or more pages.
question_type_taxonomy.cross_topic_synthesis: Integrates information from at least two topics or domains and requires a conclusion or classification, not simple fact concatenation.
question_type_taxonomy.multi_entity_comparison: Compares at least two entities on explicit dimensions using only corpus evidence.
question_type_taxonomy.complex_relation_tracking: Tracks at least three relationship layers from a person, organization, or project and distinguishes direct from indirect links.
question_type_taxonomy.distractor_disambiguation: Requires selecting the correct evidence when similar entities or a related but insufficient page could mislead.
question_type_taxonomy.unanswerable: The corpus lacks the required information; a refusal is required.

scoring_rule: answer_correct = for every group in answer_keyword_groups, at least one keyword appears in the normalized answer. For unanswerable cases, answer_correct = at least one refusal_keyword appears and no case-specific fabrication_keyword appears. All matching is case-insensitive after stripping punctuation. The fabrication guard is a lexical heuristic for refusal-plus-invention; it does not replace manual audit of unanswerable cases.
